target_customer: Smartphone and smartwatch users and wearable makers who need compact text input
problem: On-screen keyboards take up too much of small screens and are slow on wearables; Minuum shrank input to a single line.
business_model: Paid keyboard app sales plus partnerships with wearable device makers

founders.name: Will Walmsley
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO by TechCrunch 2014-02-06; the YC page lists him as Founder/CEO.

founders.name: Severin Smith
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no bio.

competitors.name: Fleksy
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as another alternative input method

competitors.name: SwiftKey
competitors.what: Predictive third party keyboard for Android and iOS
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as another alternative input method

technical_complexity.rationale: A one dimensional keyboard with prediction on Android and smartwatches rests on human computer interaction research and language modelling, started as a University of Toronto research project per a BrainStation article seen in search.

defensibility.rationale: Novel interaction design and language models, but platform keyboards could copy and no patents were found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apple allowed third party keyboards in iOS 8 in 2014 and Google kept improving its own keyboard; no source shows an incumbent copying the single line design.

market_need_then: Smartwatches such as the Samsung Galaxy Gear launched in 2013 and lacked a good input method; Minuum raised 87,354 dollars on Indiegogo, nearly nine times its goal, and worked with wearable partners.

branding.domain_note: The YC listing gives no website; the product and company names differ (Minuum, Whirlscape).

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline the little keyboard for big fingers

branding.brand_signature: The little keyboard for big fingers tagline and the single line keyboard
branding.community_and_virality: Crowdfunding campaign with nearly 10,000 backers per a PR Newswire summary in search, and reviews by Digital Trends, PhoneArena and Droid Life; no merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Minuum had a memorable tagline, crowdfunding backers and wide tech press, but the company name Whirlscape was separate and the later Dango product used a new name.

pivots.to: Dango, a deep learning emoji suggestion app
pivots.why: Not stated in sources opened; the YC page tagline names Dango and 2016 coverage (BetaKit, Android Central, MobileSyrup) describes the launch.

outcome_analysis: Whirlscape raised a 500 thousand dollar seed in February 2014 from YC, FundersClub and BDC Venture Capital after an Indiegogo campaign, and shipped Minuum on Android and wearables. It later launched Dango, an emoji suggestion app, in 2016. No shutdown, acquisition or post-mortem was found, so the cause of the inactive status is not public; the YC page lists the company as inactive while a Wefunder page for Whirlscape exists but could not be opened.
notes: Founded year 2012 comes from BrainStation and PR Newswire summaries seen in search results (June 2012); the YC page says 2014. Company Check lists a separate 125 thousand dollar seed in March 2014, a single database claim that conflicts with the 500K reported by TechCrunch and not recorded as a round. The Indiegogo amount is crowdfunding, recorded as other with the year only. ZoomInfo calls BDC the lead investor, unconfirmed. Wefunder page returned HTTP 403 so any later crowdfunding round is not recorded. Exit type is unknown because the status conflicts with Dango activity in 2016. Education and prior employers not found. No website listed on the YC listing.
